title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
summary: Given an array of stock prices where each element represents the price of a stock on the i-th day, determine the maximum profit you can achieve by completing at most two transactions.
statement: Given an array of stock prices where each element represents the price of a stock on the i-th day, determine the maximum profit you can achieve by completing at most two transactions. Ensure that you do not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously, meaning you must sell the stock before you can buy again.
constraints: Complete at most two buy-then-sell transactions. Hold at most one share, selling it before buying another. Zero or one transaction is also allowed.
reference_solution:
def stock_profit_two(prices):
    buy1 = buy2 = -prices[0]
    sell1 = sell2 = 0
    for price in prices:
        buy1 = max(buy1, -price)
        sell1 = max(sell1, buy1 + price)
        buy2 = max(buy2, sell1 - price)
        sell2 = max(sell2, buy2 + price)
    return sell2
hints: Track whether the first or second transaction has been bought or sold.
Four running states hold the best balance after buy1, sell1, buy2, and sell2.
At each price, maximize buy1 with -price, sell1 with buy1+price, buy2 with sell1-price, and sell2 with buy2+price.
The second purchase includes the first sale's profit; two independent global best trades could overlap illegally.
editorial: The four states summarize all useful histories after each day without storing a table. A purchase subtracts today's price from the best eligible cash balance; a sale adds it to the best corresponding holding balance. Keeping prior state values represents waiting. Same-day zero-length transitions cannot improve profit improperly and allow the second-sale state to represent fewer than two trades. The oracle independently enumerates every single transaction and every ordered pair of nonoverlapping transactions.

tests.explanation: Buy at 0 and sell at 3, then buy at 1 and sell at 4, for total profit 6.
One trade from 1 to 5 earns 4; using the second trade is optional.
